page.layout: One page of verse, one block of lines; a few marginal fragments at the right edge (note-like marks, not text worth transcribing as notes). Running head at top centre.

p.i: Sauromatas, i, Scifæ, doces, gelidósque Polonos,
Quos modo cœlesti renouatos Spiritus aura
Progenuit miserans, longáque a nocte reduxit:
Orcadas, & Scotia plenis pete littora velis:
Hic nuper lux illa Dei Verbúmque Salutis
Sacrum illud nostra manifesto lumine coram
Explicuit sese, hic sedes tutique receptus
Sanctus Europa exulibus profugisque parantur.
Vise anni Solisque vias, ubi nostra Canopum
Gens videt, & nostris contraria sidera cernit
Admirans, longe Europa Calpeque relictis.
A tergo, Ammerica propter, quà laguidus annū
Exiguum vertens, gelido sub sydere nobis
Sol hyemem facit, & currit breuioribus horis.
Qua patet, inque sinum pandit se diuite luco,
Brefilia: infelix supra execratáque tellus
Cannibalum, Paranas infra, Lepetisque, fonanti
Murmure gemmarum & squammis crepitanti-
bus auri,
In mare precipites, iunctosimul agmine currūt.
I, liber, & reduces iterum solare Britannos,
Post longa exilia & laqueos cineresque suorum:
Quos inter pietate grauis, venerandus, honora
Canicie, dextram medios qui latus in ignes
Coniecit, nostro fulget memorabilis auo
Crammerus: pete culta, liber, quà Sequana labit,
Qua Ligeris secat, & Rhodanus, rapidúsque Ga-
runna.
I, liber, & veteres mærens inuise tot urbes
Qua

page.notes: Marginal and edge marks at the right and left margins are not legible as text. Line-end fragments "Ga-" and "Qua" are as printed. Several words in the Latin are uncertain due to the scan's quality; the verse has been transcribed as far as legible.
